From: Chu Choi Ying
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
mpss@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
The Chinese version follows the English version of this email.
Multicultural Psychological Support Service: Counselling Service for Non-Local Students
No matter where we come from, we all desire to express our emotional needs with no barrier. Speaking in our mother tongue with someone who shares our cultural background not only allows us to better articulate ourselves but also fosters a deeper sense of understanding.
In order to support CUHK non-local students, the Wellness and Counselling Centre (WACC) of the Office of Student Affairs (OSA) offers Multicultural Psychological Support Service. This service allows students to receive counselling services in a comfortable environment.
The service is provided by St John’s Cathedral Counselling Service, and it is available to all CUHK full-time non-local students. The counsellors from St John’s Cathedral Counselling Service are capable of providing counselling services in English or Putonghua, as well as other languages including English, Putonghua, French, German, Dutch, Spanish, Hindi, Indonesian, Japanese, Portuguese, Korean, Urdu, Russian, Sindhi and Tagalog (subject to counsellor’s availability). Below are the specific details of the services provided:
Location:
St John’s Cathedral Counselling Service
Address:
10th Floor, Two Chinachem Plaza, 68 Connaught Road, Central
Website:
https://www.sjccs.hk/
Service Period:
July 2026 to June 2027
Opening hours:
9AM to 9PM Monday to Saturday, except on Public Holiday
Service Target:
All CUHK full-time non-local students, including exchange students.
Local students with extensive exposure to cultural experiences outside Hong Kong are also eligible (e.g. with international school backgrounds, or ethnic minorities born in Hong Kong).
Session:
6 counselling sessions
For more information about the Multicultural Psychological Support Service, please visit
OSA WACC website
or contact WACC staff at 3943 9951 or 3943 7208.
How can I make an appointment?
Enroll online by webform:
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13733096
If you have an urgent need to see a counsellor, you may visit WACC during office hours. The Duty Counsellor will assess your needs and make appropriate arrangements with you. If you need emotional support during non-office hours, please call the CUHK 24-hour Emotional Support Hotline at 5400 2055 (exclusively for CUHK Full-time Students and Part-time PGDE Students).
Enquiries:
Contact number: 3943 9951/ 3943 7208
Email:
mpss@cuhk.edu.hk
/
wacc@cuhk.edu.hk
Best regards,
Multicultural Psychological Support Service (MPSS)
Wellness and Counselling Centre
Office of Student Affairs
3/F Pommerenke Student Centre, The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shatin, N.T.
T: +852 3943 9951   E:
mpss@cuhk.edu.hk
多元文化心理支援服務
為非本地學生提供母語輔導服務
無論來自哪裡，我們都渴望輕鬆地表達感受。用母語與有相似文化背景的人交談，不僅讓我們能清楚表達自己，還可增強更深層次的理解。為支援非本地同學，學生事務處心理健康及輔導中心推出「多元文化心理支援服務」，讓同學可在舒服自在的情況下打開心扉。
輔導服務由中環聖約翰座堂輔導服務提供，服務對象為所有香港中文大學全日制非本地學生。輔導員除了能提供以英語或普通話為母語的輔導服務外，亦能以法語、德語、荷蘭語、西班牙語、印地語、印尼語、日語、葡萄牙語、韓語、烏爾都語、俄語、信德語和他加祿語等其他語言進行輔導。服務詳情如下：
服務提供者：
聖約翰座堂輔導服務中心
服務地址：
中環幹諾道中
68
號華懋廣場Ⅱ期
10
樓
網址：
https://www.sjccs.hk/
服務時段：
2026年7月至2027年六月
營業時間：
週一至週六上午 9 時至晚上 9 時，公眾假期除外
服務對象：
香港中文大學全日制非本地學生，包括交換生
本地學生如有豐富的非本地文化背景（如曾就讀國際學校，或在香港出生的少數族裔人士）亦可申請
輔導次數：
提供6次輔導服務
有關「多元文化心理支援服務」的詳情，請瀏覽
學生事務處心理健康及輔導中心網頁
或致電3943 9951或3943 7208向心理健康及輔導中心職員查詢。
如何預約輔導服務？
於網上預約:
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13733096
如急需與輔導員見面，可於辦公時間內到訪位於龐萬倫學生中心2樓的心理健康及輔導中心。當值的輔導員會評估同學的需要，並作出適當的安排。如欲在非辦公時間尋求情緒支援，歡迎致電中大24小時情緒支援熱線5400 2055（僅供中文大學全日制學生及兼讀制學位教師教育文憑學生使用）。

No matter where we come from, we all desire to express our emotional needs with no barrier. Speaking in our mother tongue with someone who shares our cultural background not only allows us to better articulate ourselves but also fosters a deeper sense of understanding.
In order to support CUHK non-local students, the Wellness and Counselling Centre (WACC) of the Office of Student Affairs (OSA) offers Multicultural Psychological Support Service. This service allows students to receive counselling services in a comfortable environment.
The service is provided by St John’s Cathedral Counselling Service, and it is available to all CUHK full-time non-local students. The counsellors from St John’s Cathedral Counselling Service are capable of providing counselling services in English or Putonghua, as well as other languages including English, Putonghua, French, German, Dutch, Spanish, Hindi, Indonesian, Japanese, Portuguese, Korean, Urdu, Russian, Sindhi and Tagalog (subject to counsellor’s availability). Below are the specific details of the services provided:
Location:
St John’s Cathedral Counselling Service
Address:
10th Floor, Two Chinachem Plaza, 68 Connaught Road, Central
Website:
https://www.sjccs.hk/
Service Period:
July 2026 to June 2027
Opening hours:
9AM to 9PM Monday to Saturday, except on Public Holiday
Service Target:
All CUHK full-time non-local students, including exchange students.
Local students with extensive exposure to cultural experiences outside Hong Kong are also eligible (e.g. with international school backgrounds, or ethnic minorities born in Hong Kong).
Session:
6 counselling sessions
For more information about the Multicultural Psychological Support Service, please visit
OSA WACC website
or contact WACC staff at 3943 9951 or 3943 7208.
How can I make an appointment?
Enroll online by webform:
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13733096
If you have an urgent need to see a counsellor, you may visit WACC during office hours. The Duty Counsellor will assess your needs and make appropriate arrangements with you. If you need emotional support during non-office hours, please call the CUHK 24-hour Emotional Support Hotline at 5400 2055 (exclusively for CUHK Full-time Students and Part-time PGDE Students).
Enquiries:
Contact number: 3943 9951/ 3943 7208
Email:
mpss@cuhk.edu.hk
/
wacc@cuhk.edu.hk
Best regards,
Multicultural Psychological Support Service (MPSS)
Wellness and Counselling Centre
Office of Student Affairs
3/F Pommerenke Student Centre, The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shatin, N.T.
T: +852 3943 9951   E:
mpss@cuhk.edu.hk
多元文化心理支援服務
為非本地學生提供母語輔導服務
無論來自哪裡，我們都渴望輕鬆地表達感受。用母語與有相似文化背景的人交談，不僅讓我們能清楚表達自己，還可增強更深層次的理解。為支援非本地同學，學生事務處心理健康及輔導中心推出「多元文化心理支援服務」，讓同學可在舒服自在的情況下打開心扉。

title: Recruiting Participants: [Brief Training Programme for Eating Disorders] 「进食问题短期训练计划」诚邀普通话参与者
bodyText:
Mass Mail System
Mass Mail System
Digest of CUHK Mass Mails for Undergraduate Students
»
2026/08/21
»
Announcements
Recruiting Participants: [Brief Training Programme for Eating Disorders] 「进食问题短期训练计划」诚邀普通话参与者 - Experimental Psychopathology and Psychotherapy Laboratory, Department of Psychology
From: Yanbin, XIE
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
ybxie@link.cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
招募参与者：进食问题短期训练计划
香港中文大学临床心理科学实验室团队现正推行一项针对进食问题的短期训练计划，诚邀符合资格的人士参与。
六周指导式自助练习，处理社会评价与自我批评
打破自我批评的恶性循环
找回自我肯定的正向情绪
香港中文大学校园内，全程免费
进食问题很多时候并非只是一个关于食物、身材偏好或者意志力的问题，而关乎我们如何看待自己，以及如何处理和他人的关系。目前，针对进食问题的治疗多采用认知行为取向，研究证实能有效控制非适应性进食行为的出现。本计划是团队基于实证研究开发的新训练方案，采用社会情绪取向，聚焦于处理自己与他人的关系。本项目遵循阶梯式照护模式，定位为指导式自助短期介入方案，旨在以较少的时间投入及心理负担为参加者提供支援。
训练为期6周，包括「每周1次实体会面 + 自助练习 + 线上心理评估访谈及问卷」；训练完成后1个月及6个月进行跟进评估。
「招募要求」
年满18岁或以上；普通话流利；
受进食问题困扰，例如，对进食、体重或体型有过度的关注，进食后感到强烈自责或羞愧，反复出现无法控制的暴食行为，或伴有反复出现的代偿行为（催吐、使用泻药或利尿剂、过度运动等）并因此影响日常生活或情绪；
目前并未接受其他形式的心理治疗或精神科药物治疗；
能够亲身前往香港中文大学校园参与训练。
「报名链接」

Announcements
[Brief Psychological Training Programme for Social Anxiety] Welcome Cantonese speakers  [社交焦慮短期訓練計劃] 誠邀符合條件的廣東話使用者參與 - Experimental Psychopathology and Psychotherapy Laboratory, Department of Psychology
From: Yanbin, XIE
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
ybxie@link.cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
招募參與者：社交焦慮短期介入訓練計劃
六週指導式自助練習，處理社會評價與自我批評
打破自我批評的惡性循環
找回自我肯定的正向情緒

香港中文大學校園內，全程免費
香港中文大學臨床心理科學實驗室團隊現正推行一項針對社交焦慮問題的短期介入訓練計劃，誠邀符合資格的人士參與。
社交焦慮不止影響我們如何應對社交場合，亦關乎我們如何看待自己，以及如何與他人建立聯繫。目前，社交焦慮問題的治療多採用認知行為取向，研究證實能有效改善個人在社交情境中的功能表現。本計劃則是團隊基於實證研究開發的新訓練方案，採用社會情緒取向，聚焦於處理個人與自我及他人的關係。本項目遵循階梯式照護模式 (stepped-care model)，定位為指導式自助 (guided self-help) 短期介入方案，旨在以較少的時間投入及心理負擔，為參加者提供有效支援。
訓練為期6週，包括「每週1次實體會面 + 自助練習 + 線上心理評估訪談及問卷」 ； 訓練完成後1個月和六個月進行隨訪評估
 「招募要求」
年滿18歲或以上；廣東話流利；
在社交焦慮方面感到困擾，例如在社交或公開場合強烈緊張焦慮、擔心自己被負面評價、迴避社交場合，並明顯影響工作或學習；
現時並未接受其他形式的心理治療或精神科藥物治療；
能夠親身前往香港中文大學校園參與訓練。

「參與流程」
報名後，我們將聯絡您安排篩選問卷及訪談，以確認是否適合參加本計劃，並邀請符合條件者參與訓練。

「報名連結」
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_eDNm9u2HOUkR302
如有疑問，歡迎聯絡研究團隊：cdclabcuhk@gmail.com
本計劃已獲香港中文大學–新界東醫院聯網臨床研究倫理聯席委員會審批（CUHK-NTEC CREC 2025.796）。
所有個人資料僅用作研究篩選及介入用途，並會嚴格保密。
香港中文大學臨床心理科學實驗室團隊
Experimental Psychopathology and Psychotherapy Laboratory
Recruiting Participants: Brief Psychological Training Programme for Social Anxiety
The Experimental Psychopathology and Psychotherapy Laboratory at The Chinese University of Hong Kong is currently conducting a brief intervention programme for individuals experiencing social anxiety difficulties. We invite eligible individuals to participate.
Social anxiety not only affects how we cope in social situations but also involves how we view ourselves and relate to others. While cognitive-behavioural approaches are widely used and evidence-based for treating social anxiety, our team has developed a novel training protocol grounded in empirical research that adopts a social-emotional approach, focusing on improving individuals’ relationships with themselves and with others. Following the stepped-care model, this programme is designed as a brief guided self-help intervention, aiming to provide effective support with minimal time commitment and psychological burden.
The training programme spans 6 weeks and includes:
Weekly in-person sessions (once per week)
Self-help practice exercises
Questionnaire assessments
Follow-up evaluations will be conducted one month and six months after the training.
「Eligibility Criteria」
Aged 18 or above
Fluent in Cantonese
Experiencing significant social anxiety-related distress (e.g., intense anxiety in social or public settings, fear of negative evaluation, avoidance of social situations, with noticeable impact on work or study)
Not currently receiving other forms of psychological therapy or psychiatric medication
Able to attend in-person sessions on the CUHK campus
「Procedures」
After registration, we will contact you to arrange a screening questionnaire and an interview to determine your suitability for the programme. Eligible participants will then be invited to join the training.
「Registration Link」
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_eDNm9u2HOUkR302
For enquiries, please contact our research team at: cdclabcuhk@gmail.com
This study has been approved by the Joint CUHK-NTEC Clinical Research Ethics Committee (CUHK-NTEC CREC 2025.796).
All personal data collected will be used solely for research screening and intervention purposes and will be kept strictly confidential.
Experimental Psychopathology and Psychotherapy Laboratory

title: Better Gut, Better Sleep? Gut-Brain Study | Earn up to HKD 500 「腸」通無阻，瞓得更好？「腸·腦」研究 | 最高可獲 HKD 500
bodyText:

Announcements
Better Gut, Better Sleep? Gut-Brain Study | Earn up to HKD 500 「腸」通無阻，瞓得更好？「腸·腦」研究 | 最高可獲 HKD 500 - Department of Psychiatry
From: Michael Ng
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
tsztsunng@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
近年醫學界發現，我們的腸道健康與大腦息息相關！原來「便秘」和「睡眠質素」的改變，可能是腦部退化的早期信號。為了深入了解這條神奇的「腸腦連線」，香港中文大學精神科學系睡眠研究組現正招募研究參加者。
研究對象:
年齡介乎 50 至 80 歲
關注腸道健康或者受便秘問題困擾（如排便困難、次數較少等）
沒有腦退化、精神疾病史
參加者需完成以下簡單程序：
填寫問卷 及 進行簡單面談
進行一次非入侵性睡眠檢測
記錄連續兩星期「大便日記」
進行一次結腸運輸試驗
收集一次大便樣本
參與研究費用全免，成功參與者最多可獲 HKD 500 超市禮券的津貼
如對本研究有興趣，請透過以下連結報名參加：
[網址連結:
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_eeTcY6hrKILNwhg
]
如對研究內容有任何疑問，歡迎致電 3919 7792 / 9568 9006 或 WhatsApp 9568 9006與負責研究人員聯絡、查詢詳情。謝謝
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Recent research suggests that gut health is closely linked to brain function. Changes in bowel habits (e.g. constipation) and sleep quality may even be early signs of neurodegeneration.
To better understand this “gut–brain axis, we sincerely invite you to take part in our research study.
Who can join:
Aged 50–80
Concerned about gut health or bothered by constipation
No history of dementia or psychiatric disorders
What you will do:
Complete questionnaires and a brief interview
Undergo a sleep assessment
Record a 2-week bowel diary
Complete a colonic transit time test
Collect one stool sample
Incentive:
All assessments are free of charge.
Eligible participants may receive up to HKD 500 in supermarket vouchers upon completion.
Interested? Please sign up here:
[
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_eeTcY6hrKILNwhg
]
Enquiries:
3919 7792 / 9568 9006
WhatsApp 9568 9006
View Count
For request submissions, please submit them at
https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk

/weekly/

From: SUE GAO

【Introduction】: This research study, titled “Compensation of White Matter Pathways and Networks in Chinese Children with Developmental Dyslexia in Hong Kong,” is led by Prof. Jingjing Zhao from the Department of Psychology at The Chinese University of Hong Kong.
【Description of the study】: The purpose of this study is to explore how white matter pathways in the brain may compensate for reading difficulties in Chinese-speaking children with developmental dyslexia in Hong Kong.
【Study Procedures】 ● Reading and Cognitive Assessments: Your child will participate in reading and cognitive assessments lasting approximately 30–40 minutes. You are not required to complete any of these tasks. ● Brain Imaging (MRI Scan): Your child will also undergo a magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scan lasting about 20 minutes. The MRI procedure is non-invasive, painless, radiation-free, and no sedation. Please inform the research team in advance if your child has claustrophobia, metal implants, or a pacemaker.
Target participants: Children aged 8–16 years, whose parents are native Mandarin or Cantonese speakers, are eligible to participate.
【Data Confidentiality and Usage】:All data will be handled in accordance with data protection and privacy regulations. All collected data will be anonymized and will not include identifiable information (e.g., name, ID number, contact details). Data will be used solely for academic research purposes.
針對多種神經發育學習障礙的閱讀困難跨診斷研究
現正招募：
8-16歲、廣東話為母語的兒童
（1） 正常發展或
（2）被診斷或懷疑有任何一項：
（i）自閉症
（ii）注意力缺陷
（iii）讀寫障礙
測試内容：
語言、記憶及認知能力測試
磁力共振掃描（MRI）
時間：2小时
地點：威爾士親王醫院（第一城）
合資格參與者完成所有測試後可獲得:
綜合語言能力評核報告
最高達$200 現金
兒童磁力共振影相電子版
神經指標分析報告

From: Helen Ho

- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
We are looking for enthusiastic students to join our team as helpers to visit hosiptals, facilitate follow-up and health talk flow! This flexible job opportunity is perfect for students who want to earn extra income in your spare time. This recruitment is for a project related to stroke aimed at raising public awareness about stroke rehabilitation.
Job Responsibilities:
Visit hospitals to assist in recruiting participants for research projects
Assist in promoting stroke prevention knowledge
Support the project team with simple liaison tasks
What We Offer:
Flexible Working Hours:
You can schedule your work hours around your class timetable
Training Sessions:
No prior experience is required; we will provide comprehensive training, including stroke-related knowledge and communication skills, to help you get started quickly
Requirements:
Good communication skills
Fluent in Cantonese
Proactive, willing to learn, and interested in health-related projects
Nursing students will be given priority consideration
If you’re interested in this position and want to contribute to stroke rehabilitation efforts, please complete the recruitment form:
https://forms.gle/NqGghj8crdL5nseh6

）
中文大學校園面授
本證書課程以參加國家語委普通話水平測試（PSC）為導向，旨在提高學員普通話應用水平，具體表現為：提高學員普通話朗讀能力，掌握普通話水平測試常用詞匯，掌握朗讀規定篇目的方法，讀準字音，讀通作品。同時，提高學員使用普通話所達到的流利程度和規範程度，掌握普通話水平測試應試的技巧，做好測試前的準備；並幫助參加過測試的應試人進一步提升等級，説話時，逐步做到語音標準，語調自然，表達流暢。本證書課程不是零起點課程，學員須具有基礎普通話能力。

Announcements
#Recruiting vocally healthy participants aged 18 and above to participate in an acoustic analysis study to explore the quality and characteristics of the voice (HK$150 coupon) 誠意邀請18歲或以上沒有聲線障礙的人士參與探索聲線質量和特徵的聲學分析研究 (HK$150 coupon) - Department of Otorhinolarynogology, Head and Neck Surgery
From: Rina To
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
rinato@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
香港中文大學耳鼻咽喉 頭頸外科學系現正招募十八歲或以上沒有聲線障礙的人士參與一項聲學分析的研究，旨在探究平滑化倒頻譜突出峰值 (CPPS) 的臨界值和其診斷準確性。
CPPS是一種可應用於日常對話的聲線聲學分析參數。CPPS相對於其他常用的聲學參數具有更高的診斷準確性。但是，根據文獻的報告顯示，使用不同的語言，聲線樣本類型，和軟件，都會影響到CPPS的結果。我們希望這項研究的結果能夠為臨床醫生和研究人員對聲線障礙患者進行客觀測量並為聲線評估的量化結果提供明確的參考。
招募對象：
年滿十八歲或以上
沒有聲線問題的人士
以廣東話為母語
費用：全免
評估與檢查地點：威爾斯親王醫院
研究程序及内容：
1）參加者將填寫聲線問卷， 並親臨威爾斯親王醫院接受喉纖維內視鏡檢查和聲線錄製。
2）喉纖維內視鏡檢查時能清楚看見咽喉，每次檢查需時約三十分鐘，是屬於低風險的檢查，一般只會感到輕微不適。
報名連結﹕
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/mycuform/view.php?id=4267989
參與研究，獲得獎勵：
完成聲線評估後，您可獲得港幣150元的超市現金券。
名額有限，先到先得。收到報名後，我們會再與合資格的參加者聯絡。
歡迎將此招募信息推薦給身邊有需要的家人以及朋友。
如有查詢，請與研究人員王先生（Mr. Wang）聯絡。
電郵：
zikaiwang@link.cuhk.edu.hk
The Department of Otorhinolaryngology, Head and Neck Surgery, The Chinese University of Hong Kong, is currently recruiting vocally healthy participants aged 18 and above for a study investigating the cut-off score and diagnostic accuracy of the smoothed cepstral peak prominence (CPPS) for Cantonese speakers with dysphonia.
CPPS is a parameter for acoustic analysis of voice that can be used in everyday conversation to provide a more comprehensive and realistic picture of an individual's vocal characteristics in natural communication situations. CPPS has a higher diagnostic accuracy than other commonly used acoustic parameters. However, reports in the literature indicate that the use of different languages, different types of voice samples, and different software can affect the results of the CPPS. We hope that the results of this study will provide clinicians and researchers with a clear reference for the quantitative results of objective measurement and voice assessment in patients with voice disorders.
Recruitment target:
Age 18 or above
People who do not have voice problems
Fluent in Cantonese as a native language or proficient in Cantonese
Cost: Free of charge
Location: Prince of Wales Hospital
Procedures and details of this Study:
Participants will undergo a laryngeal videostroboscopy examination and a comprehensive voice assessment at Prince of Wales Hospital.
A videostroboscopy examination can clearly observe the throat to detect whether it has structural or functional problem for speaking. Each examination takes approximately thirty minutes. It is a low-risk procedure, and participants typically only experience mild discomfort.
Registration link:
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/mycuform/view.php?id=4267989
Participate in the study and receive a reward:
After completing the voice assessment, you will receive a HK$ 150 supermarket gift card.
Limited seats available on a first-come first-served basis. We will contact you afterwards if you are suitable to join this study.
Welcome to recommend this recruitment information to your family and friends in need.
If you have any inquiries, please contact Mr. Wang.
Email:
zikaiwang@link.cuhk.edu.hk
View Count

https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk

From: Maggie Lee
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
maggielee@cuhk.edu.hk

[
新中藥方劑治療
2
型糖尿病的臨床安全性、有效性和多組評價：對
β
細胞功能和胰島素抵抗的影響】
香港中文大學內科及藥物治療學系與香港中文大學香港中西醫結合醫學研究所現正聯合進行一項為期36週，以內服中藥(沖劑)治療 2 型糖尿病人
 研究對象：18至70歲華人
沒有重大疾病，沒有服用中藥， 身體質量指數 (BMI) ≥18 kg/m²  (公斤 ÷ 米 ÷ 米)
不吸煙或已戒煙至少 12 個月，如女性目前未懷孕
患糖尿病未滿 6 年，且在過去 3 個月內未使用任何降血糖藥物（包括胰島素）治療
至少具備以下其中一項風險因素:
糖尿病家族史 (尤其父母或兄弟姐妹在40歲前診斷 )
代謝綜合症 (3高：高血糖，高血壓，高膽固醇)
超重或肥胖
脂肪肝
多囊卵巢綜合症
妊娠糖尿病病史
如不確定自己是否患有糖尿病，會安排你服用葡萄糖飲料（75 克口服葡萄糖耐量試驗）
研究內容：中西醫評估、心電圖、肝纖維化掃描、抽血檢查、填寫問卷、服用研究中藥或安慰劑等
地點：新界沙田威爾斯醫院，舊座，3 樓，3M 病房 - 糖尿及內分泌研究中心
參與研究費用全免，成功參與者可獲得高達港幣 $1,000 的津貼，名額有限，先到先得！
閣下如對本研究有興趣請透過以下連結報名參加：
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/mycuform/view.php?id=3542692
如果初步合適參與研究，負責同事將稍後聯絡你，謝謝
如對研究內容有任何疑問，歡迎致電  3505 3897 / 6937 3365 或 WhatsApp 6937 3365與負責研究人員聯絡、查詢詳情。
[Clinical safety, efficacy and multiomic evaluation of a novel Chinese Medicine formula in Type 2 diabetes: Effects on beta-cell function and insulin resistance
.]
Department of Medicine and Therapeutics and Hong Kong Institute of Integrative Medicine, CUHK are jointly conducting a 36-week clinical study on the use of oral traditional Chinese medicine (granule form) for treating type 2 diabetes.
Eligibility Criteria: Ethnic Chinese individuals aged 18 to 70 years
No major illnesses, not currently taking any traditional Chinese medicine, and with a Body Mass Index (BMI) ≥ 18 kg/m² (kg ÷ metre ÷ metre)
Non-smokers or those who have quit smoking for at least 12 months; females must not be currently pregnant
Diagnosed with type 2 diabetes for less than 6 years and have not used any glucose-lowering medications (including insulin) in the past 3 months
Must have at least one of the following risk factors:
Family history of diabetes (especially if parents or siblings were diagnosed before age of 40)
Metabolic syndrome (three highs: high blood sugar, high blood pressure, high blood cholesterol)
Overweight or obesity
Fatty liver
Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS)
History of gestational diabetes
If you are unsure whether you have diabetes, a 75g oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT) will be arranged for you.

Study Procedures Include:
Chinese and Western medical assessments, Electrocardiogram (ECG), Liver fibrosis scan, Blood tests, Questionnaire completion, Taking either the study Chinese medicine or a placebo
Location: Ward 3M, 3/F, Old Block, Diabetes and Endocrinology Research Centre, Prince of Wales Hospital, Sha Tin, New Territories
Free of charge to participate.
Successful participants may receive an allowance of up to HKD $1,000.
Limited quota – first come, first served!
Register via the following link:
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/mycuform/view.php?id=3542692
If you are eligible based on initial assessment, our research team will contact you shortly. Thank you!
For inquiries, please contact:
3505 3897 / 6937 3365
WhatsApp: 6937 3365

細胞功能和胰島素抵抗的影響】
香港中文大學內科及藥物治療學系與香港中文大學香港中西醫結合醫學研究所現正聯合進行一項為期36週，以內服中藥(沖劑)治療 2 型糖尿病人
 研究對象：18至70歲華人
沒有重大疾病，沒有服用中藥， 身體質量指數 (BMI) ≥18 kg/m²  (公斤 ÷ 米 ÷ 米)
不吸煙或已戒煙至少 12 個月，如女性目前未懷孕
患糖尿病未滿 6 年，且在過去 3 個月內未使用任何降血糖藥物（包括胰島素）治療
至少具備以下其中一項風險因素:
糖尿病家族史 (尤其父母或兄弟姐妹在40歲前診斷 )
代謝綜合症 (3高：高血糖，高血壓，高膽固醇)
超重或肥胖
脂肪肝
多囊卵巢綜合症
妊娠糖尿病病史
如不確定自己是否患有糖尿病，會安排你服用葡萄糖飲料（75 克口服葡萄糖耐量試驗）
研究內容：中西醫評估、心電圖、肝纖維化掃描、抽血檢查、填寫問卷、服用研究中藥或安慰劑等
地點：新界沙田威爾斯醫院，舊座，3 樓，3M 病房 - 糖尿及內分泌研究中心
參與研究費用全免，成功參與者可獲得高達港幣 $1,000 的津貼，名額有限，先到先得！
閣下如對本研究有興趣請透過以下連結報名參加：
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/mycuform/view.php?id=3542692
如果初步合適參與研究，負責同事將稍後聯絡你，謝謝
如對研究內容有任何疑問，歡迎致電  3505 3897 / 6937 3365 或 WhatsApp 6937 3365與負責研究人員聯絡、查詢詳情。
[Clinical safety, efficacy and multiomic evaluation of a novel Chinese Medicine formula in Type 2 diabetes: Effects on beta-cell function and insulin resistance
.]
Department of Medicine and Therapeutics and Hong Kong Institute of Integrative Medicine, CUHK are jointly conducting a 36-week clinical study on the use of oral traditional Chinese medicine (granule form) for treating type 2 diabetes.
Eligibility Criteria: Ethnic Chinese individuals aged 18 to 70 years
No major illnesses, not currently taking any traditional Chinese medicine, and with a Body Mass Index (BMI) ≥ 18 kg/m² (kg ÷ metre ÷ metre)
Non-smokers or those who have quit smoking for at least 12 months; females must not be currently pregnant
Diagnosed with type 2 diabetes for less than 6 years and have not used any glucose-lowering medications (including insulin) in the past 3 months
Must have at least one of the following risk factors:
Family history of diabetes (especially if parents or siblings were diagnosed before age of 40)
Metabolic syndrome (three highs: high blood sugar, high blood pressure, high blood cholesterol)
Overweight or obesity
Fatty liver
Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS)
History of gestational diabetes
If you are unsure whether you have diabetes, a 75g oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT) will be arranged for you.

Study Procedures Include:
Chinese and Western medical assessments, Electrocardiogram (ECG), Liver fibrosis scan, Blood tests, Questionnaire completion, Taking either the study Chinese medicine or a placebo
Location: Ward 3M, 3/F, Old Block, Diabetes and Endocrinology Research Centre, Prince of Wales Hospital, Sha Tin, New Territories
Free of charge to participate.
Successful participants may receive an allowance of up to HKD $1,000.
Limited quota – first come, first served!
Register via the following link:
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/mycuform/view.php?id=3542692
If you are eligible based on initial assessment, our research team will contact you shortly. Thank you!
For inquiries, please contact:
3505 3897 / 6937 3365
WhatsApp: 6937 3365

Announcements

From: Fung Hoi Kuen

henryfung@cuhk.edu.hk

日期：
2026 年9 月至11 月，共10 堂
（9 月：18 ；10 月：2, 9, 16, 23, 30; 11 月：6, 13, 20, 27 ）
時間：
初階 ( 白帶&黃帶): 11:30 am – 1:00 pm
進階 ( 綠帶及以上): 11:30 am – 1:30 pm
場地：
和聲書院低座一樓胡定旭演講室
課程費用：
$800
8 成出席率可獲退款
和聲書院學生退款 - $300
中大學生、職員及和聲書院校友退款 - $200
* 學員需穿著空手道袍、拳套及道袍腰帶上課，相關物品可在報名表格中選購
** 學員可在最後一課，向導師提出參加考核，考核將於課程完結後舉行
其他費用：
空手道袍和白帶 ( 必需裝備)
和聲書院學生- $200
中大學生、職員及和聲書院校友 - $300
拳套 ( 必需裝備) - $200
腳套 ( 可選) - $ 300
考試費- 可選；須獲導師認可參與考核，將於課程結束後公佈
名額：
20
導師：
馬文心女士 (Margo)
l   前空手道精英運動員2007-2022
l   最高世界排名4
l   世界超級聯賽分站銀牌
l   亞洲賽銅牌
l   東亞運動會金牌
l   香港10 年搏擊冠軍
l   中國香港空手道總會3 級教練
l   香港中文大學空手道校隊教練
l   空手道黑帶4 段
付款方式：
請透過下列方法繳費 ( 連同道袍、白帶、拳套及腳套費用) ：
網上銀行轉賬：轉賬後截圖付款紀錄，並上載至報名表格。   截圖上須清晰列明中大賬戶號碼、交易參考編號及日期
中大賬戶號碼: 293-005005-018 (HSB)
賬戶名稱: The Chinese University of Hong Kong ／香港中文大學
*** 參加者必需於第一堂開課前繳交全部費用
備註：
學員需自備毛巾及水瓶上課。
學員應協助導師進行場地設置及還原工作。
有興趣參與空手道課程的學員，請在9 月17 日前於
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13737584
報名。學員將於截止後收到書院院務室電郵通知。
如有任何問題，歡迎聯絡書院院務室何先生 (3943 1398;
khho@cuhk.edu.hk
) 。

You are going to study the skills and gain Kyu (rank qualification) under guidance of our professional trainer! All students with different levels, including beginners and experience players, are welcome to join our class with a favourable price.
Please note the course schedule below:
Date ：
Fridays from September to November 2026, 10 lessons available:
(Sep: 18 ; Oct: 2, 9, 16, 23, 30; Nov: 6, 13, 20, 27)
Time ：
Beginners (White & Yellow): 11:30 am – 1:00 pm
Advanced (Green & Above): 11:30 am – 1:30 pm
Venue ：
Anthony Wu Seminar Room, LG1/F, Lee Woo Sing College
Course Fee ：
HKD$800 (Karate Uniform Gi NOT included)
* Refund will be made to participants who reach 80% attendance:
Lee Woo Sing College students - HKD$300 refund
CUHK students / staff / WS Alumni - HKD$200 refund
Other Fees ：
Karate Uniform Gi plus White Belt (required)
$200 for LWS students
$300 for non-LWS students
Gloves (required) - $200
Foot Cover (optional) - $ 350
Examination Fee - optional; to be paid after instructor’s approval
No. of Participants (Max) ：
20
Instructor ：
Ms. MA Man Sum, Margo
l    Former Elite Karate Athlete 2007-2022
l    Highest World Ranking No. 4
l    World Premier League Silver
l    Asian Championship Bronze
l    East Asian Gold
l    National Champion 10 times
l    Certified Karate Coach level 3 & karate Referee
l    Karate Team Coach
l    Black Belt 4 Dan
Payment Method:
Please submit course fee (and uniform, belt and gloves, if any), to College Office via online payment transfer (e-banking):
After completion of payment, please save the screen capture as jpg/ png format, and attach to the WebForm . The payment record captured should include CUHK bank account no., transaction reference number and transaction date clearly
Account No.: 293-005005-018 (Hang Seng Bank)
Account Name: The Chinese University of Hong Kong
*** Participants must settle the payment before the start of first lesson
Note to participants:
Participants should bring with own towels and bottled water to attend the classes.
Participants are advised to assist the instructor in venue set-up and restoration.
Interested parties please enroll at
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13737584
before 17 September. Applicants will receive a notification email to confirm the place.
View Count
For request submissions, please submit them at
https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk

Deepen Your Practice: Free Online Info Session for "The Feeling Tone" Teacher Training!
Interested in exploring the subtle layers of Vedana (Feeling Tone) to transform reactivity into wise, compassionate action?
Join our lead trainer, Antonia Dorothea Sumbundu, alongside local trainers Prof. Stanley Chan and Mr. Ting Ka Tsun, for an exclusive interactive Zoom Information Session!
Whether you are looking to deepen your own practice or teach the new "Deeper Mindfulness" 8-week curriculum, this session will cover everything you need to know about programme structure, eligibility, and key learning outcomes.
Info Session Details:
• Date: Tuesday, 25 August 2026
• Time: 8:00 PM – 9:00 PM (Hong Kong Time)
• Format: Online via Zoom
•
RSVP for Info Session:
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/mycuform/view.php?id=4374919

Announcements
[$320 travel allowance] Recruiting aged 65 or above elderly, along with their caregivers, to join a survey on elderly physical and mental health.  [$320交通津貼] 招募年滿65歲或以上的長者及其照顧者參加問卷調查，以了解香港長者的身心健康 - JC School of Public Health and Primary Care
From: Amy Wong
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
amy.wong@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
***
中文版本
***
研究背景
香港中文大學現正進行一項有關長者身心健康的調查，從而制定一個可以測量長者健康生活品質的工具。
招募對象
長者：65歲或以上，照顧者：18歲或以上；
香港居民；
能閱讀中文及以廣東話溝通； 及
曾使用長者服務設施或入住護理之家
參與方式
如果符合上述條件，請在下方連結登記及留下相關資料以作跟進，需時約1-3分鐘。完成登記後，研究人員將於兩星期內與你聯絡，並安排你與被照顧的長者以面對面或 Zoom形式完成問卷調查。
答謝安排
問卷調查約需 10–15 分鐘。首次完成問卷後，長者與照顧者合共可獲港幣 160 元現金以作答謝。約一星期後，我們將邀請二人再次完成相同問卷，完成後可再獲合共港幣 160 元現金以作答謝。每位長者只限參加一次。
報名登記連結
:
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_3qPvrQNVMFR0vz0
研究海報：
https://drive.google.com/file/d/1uT7ZS1Me6Nv_2qnVhXH6MozHA3GMc5mU/view?usp=sharing
查詢
本研究已獲香港中文大學 — 調查及行為研究操守委員會的審批。 (參考編號: SBRE-25-0737) 。如有任何查詢，歡迎聯絡主研究員 黃麗儀教授 (電郵:
lywong@cuhk.edu.hk
) 或研究員黃小姐 (Amy) / 張小姐 (Annie) (電話: 2252-8408 / 2252-8404) 。
名額有限！先到先得！
歡迎轉發此訊息給您的家人及朋友！
***
English version
***
S
tudy Background
The JC School of Public Health and Primary Care at The Chinese University of Hong Kong is currently conducting a survey on the physical and mental health of older adults in Hong Kong to develop a tool in measuring their health-related quality of life in Hong Kong.
Target Group
Elderly: Aged 65 or above; Caregiver: 18 years old or above;
Hong Kong residents;
Able to read Chinese and communicate in Cantonese; and
Has ever used elderly service facilities or nursing homes.
How to Participate
If you meet the above criteria, please complete the registration form in around 1-3 minutes. After registration, our staff will contact you within two weeks and arrange an in-person/ Zoom interview for you and the elderly participant to complete the questionnaire.
Appreciation
The survey takes about 10-15 minutes. Upon completion, you and the elderly participant will receive a total of HK$160 cash as a token of appreciation. You and the elderly participant will also be invited to take the same follow-up survey in around one week, and you will receive an additional HK$160 cash after finishing it. Each elderly participant may only participate once.
Registration L
ink:
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_3qPvrQNVMFR0vz0
Study
Poster:
https://drive.google.com/file/d/1uT7ZS1Me6Nv_2qnVhXH6MozHA3GMc5mU/view?usp=sharing
Contact Us
This study has been approved by the Survey and Behavioural Research Ethics Committee (Ref: SBRE-25-0737). Should you have any enquiries, please contact the Principal Investigator Prof. Eliza Wong (E-mail: lywong@cuhk.edu.hk) or researchers Ms. Amy Wong or Ms. Annie Cheung (Tel: 2252-8408 / 2252-8404).
Limited quotas only! First come, first served!
Feel free to share this invitation with your family and friends!

https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk

/weekly/

title: AI ‘as’ and ‘for’ Education: Integrating AI Ethics in Curriculum Design and AI Tool Demonstration
bodyText:

»
2026/08/14
»
Seminars / Forums / Programmes / Workshops
AI ‘as’ and ‘for’ Education: Integrating AI Ethics in Curriculum Design and AI Tool Demonstration  - CUHK Centre for Bioethics
From: CUHK Centre for Bioethics
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
bioethics@med.cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
[This email is sent on behalf of the CUHK Centre for Bioethics and the Centre for Learning Enhancement And Research, CUHK.]
Dear Colleagues,
As Artificial Intelligence (AI) rapidly drives the digital transformation of healthcare, shaping a university curriculum that balances advanced technical literacy with robust moral foundations is more essential than ever.
We are pleased to invite you to our upcoming event, “
AI ‘as’ and ‘for’ Education: Integrating AI Ethics in Curriculum Design and AI Tool Demonstration”
, co-organized by the
CUHK Centre for Bioethics (CBIOE)
and the
Centre for Learning Enhancement And Research (CLEAR)
. This event will explore approaches to integrating AI ethics into curriculum design and share practical insights and tips for colleagues interested in incorporating in their respective disciplines.
AI ‘as’ and ‘for’ Education: Integrating AI Ethics in Curriculum Design and AI Tool Demonstration
Date
21 August 2026 (Friday)
Time
3:00pm – 4:30pm
Venue
LT 9, Yasumoto International Academic Park (YIA), CUHK
Register Now
Click
HERE
Abstract
This talk discusses the development of a modern curriculum for Year 1 and 2 (pre-clinical) students in clinical medicine, modified from traditional frameworks to better align with the digital transformation of healthcare. The curriculum embeds AI literacy into both the technical and ethical foundations of early medical training. This includes a course that condenses traditional mathematics and physics, focusing on clinically relevant applications in statistics, AI, bioinformatics, and biomedical engineering. Additionally, AI-specific case studies are integrated into the existing Bioethics course to address challenges such as algorithmic bias and diagnostic accountability. By evolving these early-stage pre-clinical frameworks, the talk illustrates how education in clinical medicine can move beyond traditional models to ensure students are prepared for the technical and moral complexities of modern, technology-driven practice.
Speakers & Moderators
Speakers
AI Ethics as Education
Integrating AI into the Pre-Clinical Curriculum for Clinical Medicine
Professor Eunice CHAN
, Assistant Professor, The Chinese University of Hong Kong (Shenzhen)
AI Tools for Education (Demonstration*)
Professor Qi DOU
, Associate Professor, Department of Computer Science and Engineering, Faculty of Engineering, CUHK
*
Demonstration will be available.
Participants are welcome to prepare a single PPT slide to try out the AI platform.
Moderators
Dr. Ann LAU
, Co-Director, CUHK Centre for Bioethics; Principal Lecturer, School of Biomedical Sciences, Faculty of Medicine, CUHK
Professor Paul LAM
, Associate Professor, Centre for Learning Enhancement And Research, CUHK
please visit
HERE
for further details and updates.
Come join us for a critical conversation on shaping an AI‑enhanced, ethics‑grounded future for education—where technology serves both learning and human values!
Best regards,
CUHK Centre for Bioethics and Centre for Learning Enhancement And Research

Events / Activities
Science in the Public Service 2026｜MoCC Programme Highlights 「科學為民」服務巡禮2026｜MoCC精彩活動 - Social Responsibility and Sustainable Development Office
From: Jockey Club Museum of Climate Change (MoCC)
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
mocc@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
「科學為民」服務巡禮2026｜MoCC精彩活動
「科學為民」服務巡禮將於今年八月至十二月舉行，以「『科學為民』二十載，科創求變惠民生」為主題。聯合政府多個部門及其他機構舉辦活動，向市民介紹政府部門及相關機構的科學工作，以及如何應用科技提供公眾服務。
作為參與機構之一，中大賽馬會氣候變化博物館（MoCC）今年將繼續響應「科學為民」服務巡禮。除了舉辦廣受歡迎的博物館及校園生態導賞外，更將聯同香港中文大學物理系攜手推出科普講座及科學體驗活動，一同探索科學的奧妙，了解科學與創新科技如何應對氣候挑戰，共創更具韌性的未來。
MoCC精彩活動：
https://www.mocc.cuhk.edu.hk/zh-tw/news/2026/1437-sips2026-ch
Science in the Public Service 2026｜MoCC Programme Highlights
Science in the Public Service (SIPS) will be held from August to December this year under the theme ‘20 Years of “Science in the Public Service”: Improving Livelihood through Science and Innovation’. Jointly organized by the government bureaux/departments and other organizations, the campaign aims to promote their scientific work and how technological applications are being applied to the provision of public services.
As one of the participating organizations, the MoCC will continue supporting the SIPS this year. In addition to the popular museum and campus eco-guided tours, the MoCC will join hands with CUHK Department of Physics to present a series of public lectures and hands-on science activities. Explore the wonders of science and discover how science and innovative technologies can help address climate challenges, building a more resilient future together.
MoCC programme highlights:
https://www.mocc.cuhk.edu.hk/en-gb/news/2026/1438-sips2026-en

「中大生態月2026」活動已開放報名
國家自2023年起將每年8月15日定為全國生態日，旨在提高社會生態文明和環境保護意識，促進自然保育工作。為了響應一年一度的全國生態日，香港中文大學社會責任及可持續發展處、賽馬會氣候變化博物館、生命科學學院、建築學院、珊瑚學院、PI Centre、以及聯合國可持續發展解決方案網絡香港地區分會（SDSN香港）將於8月15日至31日，舉辦一系列相關活動，透過不同形式的專題展覽、講座和生態導賞活動，推動共同關注生態保育，以行動保護環境。
活動現已開放報名，名額有限，歡迎大家踴躍參加！
詳情及報名：
https://www.mocc.cuhk.edu.hk/zh-tw/news/2026/1435-cuhk-ecology-month-2026-ch
‘CUHK Ecology Month 2026’ Activities Now Open for Registration
Since 2023, the establishment of National Ecology Day on 15 August has marked a new stage for ecological civilisation in China. It aims at raising public awareness of ecological civilization, environmental protection, and promoting nature conservation efforts.
In response to this annual National Ecology Day, CUHK’s Social Responsibility and Sustainable Development Office, Jockey Club Museum of Climate Change, School of Life Sciences, School of Architecture, Coral Academy, PI Centre, as well as SDSN Hong Kong, will organize a series of related activities from 15 to 31 August, including themed exhibition, talk and ecological tours to foster a collective focus on biodiversity conservation and protect the environment through action.
Registration is now open. Places are limited, don’t miss out and sign up now!

【中大生態月2026】「珊瑚寶寶的成長日記：珊瑚學院的修復技術與最新進展」專題講座
本次講座將探討在高度城市化及高混濁度海域中進行珊瑚修復所面臨的獨特機遇與挑戰。崔佩怡教授將詳細介紹珊瑚繁殖及培育策略。講座其中一個重點是成功於實驗室培育珊瑚幼體，並將幼體移植至海洋環境後成長至具繁殖能力的階段，以及總結香港珊瑚修復工作的主要成果與重要啟示，並探討未來如何擴大修復規模，於城市化沿岸環境中建立更具韌性的珊瑚生態系統。
日期：2026年8月21日（星期五）
時間：下午12時30分至1時30分
地點：賽馬會氣候變化博物館（香港中文大學康本國際學術園8樓）
語言：廣東話
報名及詳情：
https://www.mocc.cuhk.edu.hk/zh-tw/news/2026/1435-cuhk-ecology-month-2026-ch
【CUHK Ecology Month 2026】‘Coral Baby Growth Diary: Restoration Techniques and Latest Advances at the Coral Academy’ Talk
This talk will focus on the unique opportunities and challenges of coral restoration in highly urbanized, turbid settings. Professor Apple Chui will detail coral breeding and propagation strategies. A key highlight is the successful lab-based rearing of coral larvae, with outplanted juveniles reaching reproductive size and successful spawning events documented in recent years in Tolo Harbour and Channel. The talk will synthesize key lessons learned and discuss the path forward for scaling coral restoration and building resilient coral ecosystems in urban coastal environments.
Date: 21 August 2026 (Friday)
Time: 12:30 pm – 1:30 pm
Venue: Jockey Club Museum of Climate Change (Yasumoto International Academic Park 8/F, The Chinese University of Hong Kong)
Language: Cantonese
Registration and details:

Lecture Series in Honour of Professor Jao Tsung-i: Reflection and Truth in Jao’s Scholarship
Professor Jao Tsung-i (1917–2018), renowned for his profound erudition in both the artistic and humanistic spheres East and West, had pioneered numerous research innovations. To commemorate the 110th anniversary of his birth, the “Lecture Series in Honour of Professor Jao Tsung-i” is co-organized by the Institute of Chinese Studies at The Chinese University of Hong Kong (CUHK), Jao Tsung-I Petite Ecole at the University of Hong Kong (HKU), Jao Tsung-I Academy of Sinology at Hong Kong Baptist University, Fung Ping Shan Library at HKU, and Hok Hoi Library. The three upcoming lectures, themed “Reflection and Truth in Jao’s Scholarship” and hosted by the Institute of Chinese Studies, will be held at CUHK on 12 September, 19 September, and 3 October.

香港中文大學手語及聾人研究中心招募研究參與者
香港中文大學手語及聾人研究中心現正進行一項探討中文閱讀模式的研究，誠邀符合以下條件的人士參與：

LEaPP Lab

第二語言學習經驗

您需要：
目前為
香港中文大學本科生
；
年滿18歲；
母語為廣東話（Cantonese）
；

填寫一份簡短的
背景問卷

20–30分鐘的線上訪談
。
訪談將以輕鬆的形式進行，主要了解您在第二語言學習中的個人經驗和感受。

完成背景問卷及線上訪談的參與者將獲得
HKD $50
，以感謝您的時間與支持。

只招募少量參與者
。符合研究條件的參與者將按報名先後次序聯絡，
名額有限，先到先得
。

zhenyizhou@cuhk.edu.hk
感謝您的參與與支持！
香港中文大學教育心理學系
LEaPP Lab

CUHK Research Recruitment | Join an Online Interview and Receive HKD $50!
The
LEaPP Lab, Department of Educational Psychology, The Chinese University of Hong Kong (CUHK)
, is currently recruiting undergraduate students for a research study on
second language learning experiences
.
Through a brief background questionnaire followed by an online interview, we hope to better understand university students' experiences and feelings during second language learning.
1. Eligibility
You are eligible to participate if you:
Are currently an
undergraduate student at CUHK
;
Are aged 18 or above;
Are a
native Cantonese speaker
; and
Have experience learning a second language (e.g., English).
2. What Will You Do?
Participants will be asked to:
Complete a brief
background questionnaire
; and
Participate in a
20–30-minute online interview
.
The interview will be informal and will mainly focus on your experiences and feelings related to second language learning.
3. Participation Reward
Participants who complete both the background questionnaire and the online interview will receive
HKD $50
as a token of appreciation for their time and contribution.
4. Limited Places and Deadline
Only a
small number of participants
will be recruited. Eligible participants will be contacted on a
first-come, first-served basis
, subject to the recruitment criteria.

Registration deadline: 20 August 2026
5. How to Participate
Please complete the brief background questionnaire and register your interest through the link below:
https://esurvey.psy.cuhk.edu.hk/jfe/form/SV_bE4IovsqrgWaTfo
Contact Us:
If you have any questions, please feel free to contact the research team:
zhenyizhou@cuhk.edu.hk
Thank you for your participation and support.

Department of Educational Psychology
The Chinese University of Hong Kong

[Register Now]  Jockey Club Sleep Well Project Finale cum International Conference 2026  - Department of Psychiatry
From: Winifred Wong
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
jcsleepwell@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
Dear Colleagues and Friends,
We cordially invite you and your colleagues to the Jockey Club Sleep Well Project Finale cum International Conference 2026 organized by the Department of Psychiatry, Faculty of Medicine, CUHK.
The conference will bring together sleep medicine specialists, academics, and frontline healthcare professionals to share the latest research and clinical advances. Through this conference, you will be equipped with evidence-based knowledge and practical skills in sleep health, with a focus on CBT-I directly from both local and world leaders. This conference brings us altogether to create strong interdisciplinary collaborations and promote coordinated, person-centered care for sleep health service users.
Conference Details
Date: 14 September 2026
Time: 11:00-18:30
Venue: LT1, Cheng Yu Tung Building, CUHK, Shatin, NT, HK
Format: In-Person or Zoom
Free Registration
Language: Primarily Conducted in English
Highlights
• Keynote lectures by internationally renowned sleep medicine experts, including Prof. Charles M. Morin, Prof. Yuichi Inoue, and Prof. Lin Lu.
• Cutting-edge research and clinical practice sharing on insomnia.
• Potential and challenges in integrating CBT-I community-based primary care with emerging technologies.
Accreditation
CPD (HKSWA, 4 Points) | CME (HKCPsych, 5 Points)
CEU (HKPS; Pending) | CME (HKAM & MCHK, 3-5 Points; Pending)
We appreciate your confirmation of attendance by 5 September 2026 via the following link:
https://forms.cloud.microsoft/r/w4AZhK5Lnm

https://conference.jcsleepwell.com
If you have any inquiries or require assistance, please feel free to contact us. Looking forward to your participation!

bodyText:

Announcements
【Earn HK$500 coupon】 Recruiting adults (aged 18-65) to participate in research on online therapy for insomnia 【可獲得 500元現金券】招募成年人 (18-65歲)參與失眠的數碼化治療研究 - Psychiatry
From: Charis
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
mastersleep@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
你是否經常在床上輾轉難眠，夜醒或早醒？你並不孤單——許多人都面臨著同樣的問題。我們誠邀您參與研究，讓專業數碼化治療助你改善睡眠！
研究目的
本研究旨在評估市民對數碼化失眠認知行為治療聊天機器人的遵從性，以及其對改善睡眠問題的效果。
治療方式
· 由專業臨床心理學家及精神科醫生設計的電子化治療
· 完全免費
參與資格
· 18至65歲能說廣東話流利溝通（能流利閱讀並理解廣東話）的香港居民
· 在過去一個月內，每週至少三晚出現睡眠困擾
· 最近四周或以上無需長期服藥
參與研究，獲得獎勵！
完成所有治療及後續測試後，您可獲得高達500港幣。
如何加入？
請點擊以下連結進行註冊，並回答幾條簡單問題。研究員將聯絡適合的參加者，詳細解釋研究內容：
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_4UPFh054GtJGXX0
聯絡我們
如有任何疑問，請於辦公時間內致電 6115-0322 與研究助理聯絡。
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Do you often toss and turn in bed, wake up frequently at night, or wake up too early? You are not alone—many people experience the same challenges. We invite you to participate in our study and explore professional digital treatment to improve your sleep!
Purpose of the Study
This research aims to evaluate the public’s adherence to a digital insomnia cognitive behavioural therapy chatbot and assess its effectiveness in improving sleep problems.
Treatment Method
· A professionally designed digital therapy created by clinical psychologists and psychiatrists
· Completely free of charge
Eligibility Criteria
· Hong Kong residents aged 18 to 65 who can speak in Cantonese fluently, read and understand Cantonese
· Experienced sleep disturbances at least 3 nights per week in the past month
· No need for long-term medication for the past four weeks or more.
Receive Rewards for Participating!
Upon completion of all treatment sessions and follow-up assessments, participants will receive up to HKD 500.
How to Join?
Click the link below to register and answer a few simple questions. Our researchers will contact suitable participants to provide further details:
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_4UPFh054GtJGXX0
Contact Us
If you have any questions, please call 6115-0322 during office hours to speak with our research assistants.

title: Join the Yung Shue Au Cultural and Sha Tau Kok Tour and Sharing at Sha Tau Kok Public Library!!!! 8月免費活動 - 齊來參加榕樹凹文化與沙頭角導賞及沙頭角公共圖書館分享
bodyText:

Events / Activities
Join the Yung Shue Au Cultural and Sha Tau Kok Tour and Sharing at Sha Tau Kok Public Library!!!! 8月免費活動 - 齊來參加榕樹凹文化與沙頭角導賞及沙頭角公共圖書館分享 - School of Architecture
From: Reimagining Yung Shue Au
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
ysa-cuhk@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
榕樹凹文化與沙頭角導賞及沙頭角公共圖書館分享
Yung Shue Au Cultural & Sha Tau Kok Tour and Sharing at Sha Tau Kok Public Library
活動詳情 / Activity Details
日期 / Date：2026年8月19日(星期三)  / 19 August 2026 (Wed)
時間 / Time ：1230 - 1600
地點 / Venue：榕樹凹、沙頭角及沙頭角公共圖書館 / Yung Shue Au, Sha Tau Kok and Sha Tau Kok Public Library
集合地點 / Meeting Point：沙頭角避風塘 Sha Tau Kok Typhoon Shelter
https://share.google/POni3sD7Hm9uTNH64
費用 / Fee：全免 / Free of charge
名額 / Quota：12
報名 / Registration
：
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13737301
如活動受天氣影響而取消，將順延至一星期後（8月26日）舉行，其他安排維持不變。
If the event is cancelled due to adverse weather conditions, it will be postponed for one week (26 August 2026), while all other arrangements will remain unchanged.
About / 簡介:
中大建築學院將與沙頭角公共圖書館合辦「榕樹凹文化與沙頭角導賞 及 沙頭角公共圖書館分享活動」。參加者將先由榕樹凹文化大使帶領走訪榕樹凹，認識其當地文化與歷史景點。其後走訪沙頭角禁區，了解沙頭角禁區發展，再前往沙頭角公共圖書館，由助理館長江晉賢先生介紹與沙頭角及榕樹凹相關的館藏書籍，從不同角度加深對兩地文化與歷史的了解。分享環節更會介紹香港公共圖書館的電子書館藏，讓參加者可隨時隨地在線上閱讀。
The CUHK School of Architecture is collaborating with the Sha Tau Kok Public Library to present the “Yung Shue Au Cultural Guided Tour and Sha Tau Kok Public Library Sharing Session.” Participants will begin with a guided tour at Yung Shue Au, led by the Yung Shue Au Cultural Ambassadors, to explore the village’s local culture and historical landmarks. The tour will then continue to the Sha Tau Kok Frontier Closed Area, where participants will learn about the architecture and development of Sha Tau Kok. The programme will then continue at the Sha Tau Kok Public Library, where Assistant Librarian Mr. Alferd Kong Chun-yin will introduce library collections related to Sha Tau Kok and Yung Shue Au, offering deeper insights into the history and culture of both areas. The sharing session will also introduce the Hong Kong Public Libraries’ e book collections, enabling participants to access online reading resources anytime and anywhere.
注意 / Notice：
參加者需自行安排來往沙頭角之交通
Participants should arrange their own transportation to Sha Tau Kok。
參加者需自行上網申請邊境禁區許可證：
Participants must apply for the Closed Area Permit online themselves:
https://www.es.police.gov.hk/
是次活動是香港中文大學建築學院「重塑榕樹凹故事」項目的一部分，並由鄉郊保育辦公室、鄉郊保育資助計劃資助。
This activity is a part of "Re-telling the Yung Shue Au Story", a project by CUHK School of Architecture, sponsored by the  Countryside Conservation Office and Countryside Conservation Funding Scheme.
View Count
For request submissions, please submit them at
https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
Copyright © 2013. All Rights Reserved. The Chinese University of Hong Kong.
/weekly/

【
World
Café:
My second home, Hong Kong
】
What was it like when you first arrived in Hong Kong? Exciting? Uncertain? Full of hope?
Living and working far from home is not always easy. There are language differences, cultural adjustments, and moments of homesickness. But there are also friendships, shared laughter, and small victories that make this city feel a little more familiar each day.
We invite  Non-Cantonese Speakers living in Hong Kong to join us for a warm and welcoming sharing gathering.
Come meet new friends, share your journey, and connect with others who understand your experience.
Different backgrounds. Different stories. One shared city.
Because no matter where we come from, Hong Kong can be our home too.⏱
【世界咖啡館：香港 也是我家】  圍埋傾計第三場
你剛到香港時是什麼樣的？ 興奮？ 不確定？ 充滿希望？
在離家很遠的地方生活和工作並不總是那麼容易。 有語言差異、文化適應和思鄉的時候。 但也有友誼、笑聲和得著，讓這座城市每天都感覺更加熟悉。
我們誠意邀請外藉居港人加入我們，共同參加這場溫暖的分享會。
來認識新朋友，分享你的旅程，並與和你有共同經歷的人聯繫。
不同的背景。 不同的故事。 一個共同的都市。⏱
What is World Café?
World Café is a discussion format that generates group wisdom through flexible small group discussions, sincere conversations, and relaxed atmosphere. It regards dialogue as a core process from a new perspective, creating a conversational context that encourages participants to open the conversation barrier, fully engage in dialogue, explore issues together, and develop deep thinking. During the conversation, participants not only express their own opinions, but more importantly, listen to the other person, and then recombine through connections to find new perspectives or blind spots that they have never noticed before, thereby forming consensus and insights, and finding new opportunities for action.
甚麼是世界咖啡館 (World Café) ？
世界咖啡館 (World Café) 是一種在輕鬆的氛圍中，透過彈性的小團體討論，真誠對話，產生團體智慧的討論方去式。它以全新的角度把對話當作一個核心流程，透過 匯談情境的營造，讓參加者都願意打開話閘子，全心投入對話，共同探索議題，發展深層思考。在談話的過程中，參與者不僅僅是表達自己看法，更重要的是聆聽對方，然後透過連結重新組合，找到新的觀點或從未察覺的盲點，進而形成共識與洞見，找到新的行動契機。
Event Information
◊ Date | August 28, 2026 (Friday)
◊ Time | 7pm to 9pm
◊ Location | Luk Heung Campus, Tai Po (Google Map：
https://maps.app.goo.gl/mPfJRAToYYokCJk59
）
◊ Target |   Non-Cantonese Speakers living in Hong Kong or any interested individuals!
◊ Quota | 8-20 people
◊ Fee | HK$50 (including light F&B)
◊ Registration |
https://forms.gle/6uearJM4sQqKiyEm6
If you have any inquiries, please feel free to check on WhatsApp+852 3943 6582.
||
Partner/Host:
Shirley Lam (@ worldcafecat): Shirley is a facilitation advocate dedicated to making it easier for others to learn and apply guidance. By writing the LinkedIn newsletter 'Facilitation Snippet' and hosting the World Café event, we aim to spark meaningful conversations. World Caf é CAT is a spontaneous community program that organizes "World Cafe" themed events in local small shops and spaces, allowing participants to participate in discussions, listen to their own ideas, stories of others, and gather collective wisdom while exploring and supporting the sustainable operation of community spaces. Since December 2023, over 65 events have been held.
合作夥伴/主持：
Shirley Lam (@worldcafecat)：Shirley是一位促進引導 (facilitation) 倡議者，致力於讓他人更容易學習與應用引導。透過撰寫 LinkedIn 電子報《Facilitation Snippet》，並主持世界咖啡（World Café）活動，以激發有意義的對話。World Café CAT是一個自發的社區計劃，透過在本地小店、空間舉辦不同主題的「世界咖啡館」(World Cafe) ，讓參加者參與討論，聆聽自己的想法、他人的故事，和凝聚大家的集體智慧之餘，發掘及支持社區空間的持續營運。由2023年12月開始，至今已舉辦超過 65場活動。
Note:
- Due to limited space in the venue, if there is a high demand for registration, we will allocate spots through random drawing.
- Successful applicants will receive a WhatsApp confirmation notification; If no response is received by then, it will be considered as unsuccessful registration.
- During the event, photography will be conducted for recording and promotional purposes, and attendees will be deemed to have agreed to the organizer's use of their portrait. The image copyright belongs to Luk Heung Commons.
備註：
- 場地空間有限，如報名踴躍，我們將以隨機抽籤方式分配名額。
- 成功報名者會收到 WhatsApp 確認通知；若屆時未收到回覆，則視為未能成功報名。
- 活動期間將進行攝錄作紀錄及宣傳用途，出席者即視為同意主辦機構使用其肖像。影像版權歸「Luk Heung Commons」所有。
⭐ ⭐ ⭐ ⭐ ⭐ ⭐ ⭐ ⭐ ⭐ ⭐ ⭐
About the Project
關於計劃
Luk Heung Commons
is a 30-month culture-led placemaking project starting in at Luk Heung Campus, Tai Po. Funded by ZeShan Foundation, the project is delivered through a strategic collaboration between Happy Ageing Lab Foundation (HALF) and Evangelical Lutheran Church Social Service – Hong Kong (ELCSS-HK). The project aims to transform the existing Luk Heung Campus into Luk Heung Commons, a community hub that connects people, builds community capacity, and promotes well-being through creative, participatory means. Luk Heung Commons will serve as a collaborative platform for creative community-based practices to develop capacity and resources in the community for promoting positive neighbourhood transformation. This project represents the coming to life of a long-held vision: a physical and social space where residents can meet, create, share resources, and weave resilient bonds of mutual support and care.
六鄉 Commons  是一項由2026年起為期 30 個月的社區營造計劃。計劃以大埔六鄉學習園地作為社區據點，由擇善基金會資助，並由樂齡實驗室（HALF）聯同基督教香港信義會社會服務部（ELCSS-HK）共同主辦。我們致力透過藝術文化，發掘並放大社區資源與潛能，與街坊共創及推動社區活動、記錄在地故事，將園地轉化為充滿活力且能提升居民身心健康的社區協作空間，深化社區連結和力量，為社區鄰里帶來積極的轉變 。長遠旨在營造一個結合社區資源與社交功能的「社區聚腳點」，讓居民在此相遇、創作、共享資源，織出一張互助互惠的堅韌網絡。
⭐ ⭐ ⭐ ⭐ ⭐ ⭐ ⭐ ⭐ ⭐ ⭐ ⭐

Announcements
Student Helper Recruitment for Chronic Disease Health App Development! 【招募 Student Helpers】一齊開發慢性病健康 App！ - Centre for Health System and Policy Research, JC School of Public Health and Primary Care
From: Jonathan Ma Chun Hei
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
jonathanma@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
We are looking for enthusiastic students to join our health app development team! This job opportunity is perfect for students who want to be involved in health tech and earn extra income.
Project Background
We are developing an AI-enabled Patient Decision Aid, an app for elderly diabetic patients. We currently have a working web-based prototype and are looking for student helpers to assist with UI design and conversion to native iOS and Android apps.
Responsibilities
Assist with UI/UX design for the app (based on the existing web prototype)
Support development of the mobile app (iOS & Android), including core functions such as user registration/login, vitals logging, AI chatbot functions, and backend data storage
Work with the development team to refine features and troubleshoot issues during development
Requirements:
Currently enrolled student, preferably in
Computer Science, Information Systems, Design
, or related fields
Experience with UI/UX design tools (e.g., Figma) and/or mobile app development (iOS/Android, React Native, or Flutter)
Able to work independently and communicate progress regularly
Proactive, eager to learn, and interested in health-related projects
Interest in health tech / elderly care applications is a
PLUS
​
If you are interested in this position, please complete the registration form:
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_2gjznwR9CYSeSCG
Our team will contact you shortly!

[Message from the Department of Geography and Resource Management]
Secure your GRM Proficiency Certificates!
Broaden your horizons with our GRM courses! Non-major students who enroll in at least three of our GRM offerings have the unique opportunity to earn the
Proficiency Certificate in Geography
—or unlock deeper expertise with specialized certificates by completing select courses:
Proficiency Certificate in Human Geography
Proficiency Certificate in Smart City and Sustainability
Proficiency Certificate in Geo-spatial Data Science
These credentials amplify your academic and professional profile in high-impact fields. Don’t miss this chance to stand out!
For more information, please visit:
https://www.grm.cuhk.edu.hk/en/ug/proficiency-certificates/introduction/
Minor Programme in Geography and Resource Management
GRM Department also offers a minor programme in Geography and Resource Management. Students are required to complete a minimum of 18 units of courses, with at least 6 units of courses at 3000 level or above. You may visit our Department’s website at
https://www.grm.cuhk.edu.hk/en/ug/programmes/overview/
for more information.

title: The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Chung Chi College 75th Anniversary “Ink Echoes: A Shared Path with Kan Tai-keung and Students” 香港中文大學崇基學院七十五週年校慶「師我．我師 - 靳埭強師生畫展」
bodyText:

Events / Activities
The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Chung Chi College 75th Anniversary “Ink Echoes: A Shared Path with Kan Tai-keung and Students” 香港中文大學崇基學院七十五週年校慶「師我．我師 - 靳埭強師生畫展」 - Chung Chi College
From: Jennifer Ng
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
jenniferng@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
傳統水墨絕不沉悶。在孩童筆下，「點、線、面」化作游魚、花鳥與小屋，甚至能以破筆揮灑出流暢山水。當代水墨畫家和平面設計師靳埭強博士融匯東西方美學。近年，他將師承自香港「新水墨運動」奠基者呂壽琨的「師古、師自然、師我」心法，轉化為啟迪孩童的美學泉源，引導外孫女阮迎及多位小小藝術家觀察日常、大膽創新。
本次師生展以「師我．我師」為題，呈現靳博士的新作、學生佳作與教學心得，深刻體現大師與孩童互為老師、共同成長的「教學相長」精神。
展覽主題亦與崇基學院之育人理念互相呼應，學院致力推動全人教育，重視師生同行。適逢崇基創校七十五周年，學院特邀靳氏師生聯袂展出，作為校慶展覽之一。展覽既見證薪火相傳的精神，也寄託對未來的期盼，透過藝術啟迪創意、涵養人文。
Traditional ink is far from lifeless. Beneath a child’s playful brush, simple dots, lines, and washes bloom into darting fish and quiet cottages, while even a frayed brush sweeps across paper to release the flowing spirit of mountains and rivers.
Contemporary master Dr. Kan Tai-keung has long blended Eastern aesthetics with Western design thinking. Channelling the "learning from tradition, nature, and self" philosophy of New Ink Movement pioneer Lui Shou-kwan, he transforms it into a wellspring of inspiration, guiding his granddaughter, Xenia Yuen, and other young artists to observe the everyday and paint with boundless imagination.
Under the theme "Ink Echoes: A Shared Path" (師我．我師), this joint exhibition showcases Dr. Kan’s latest creations alongside student works, beautifully capturing the spirit of mutual learning and growth.
The theme of this exhibition also resonates deeply with Chung Chi College’s educational mission and commitment to whole-person development, where holistic education and the value of learning through teacher-student companionship have long been cherished. In celebration of Chung Chi College’s 75th Anniversary, the College is honoured to invite Dr. Kan and his students to present their works. Through this exhibition, the enduring spirit of generational continuity is brought to the fore, while aspirations for the future are reflected. Through art, the exhibition seeks to inspire creativity and cultivate humanistic values.

From: Donald Liu
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
donaldliu@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
靜觀課程對有慢性壓力的長者的微生物群成效研究: 隨機對照試驗
Effects of mindfulness-based training on the microbiome of older adults with chronic stress: A randomised controlled trial
現正誠邀合資格人士報名參加
We are now recruiting participants to join our programme.
賽馬會公共衛生及基層醫療學院 現誠邀60歲以上人士參加一項靜觀課程研究
研究將會探討靜觀課程對有慢性壓力的長者的微生物群的影響。
很多長者受慢性壓力困擾，如未能適當處理壓力，對他們的心理及生理皆有嚴重影響。研究發現慢性壓力會破壞腸道微生物群的平衡。靜觀證實可有效改善心理健康，卻甚少研究探究靜觀課程如何改善參與者的微生物群。這項研究將在社區招募138名年滿60歲人士，邀請他們參與為長者而設的靜觀課程與健康教育控制課程，比較兩者於改善壓力、負面情緒及腸道微生物的成效。
參加者將會被隨機分派入兩組其中一組：
a) 靜觀練習組：
分派入本組的參加者將接受為期八周，每週一次，每次大約一小時三十分鐘的靜觀課程。每堂靜課程將會錄音，以作審視課程的保真度。
b) 健康教育組：
分派入本組的參加者會接受為期八周，每週一次，每次大約一小時三十分鐘的健康教育課程，課程內容包括營養，運動，維持生活習慣。每堂靜課程將會錄音，以作審視課程的保真度。
招募對象:
i) 年齡60歲以上;
ii) 能聽講廣東話;
iii) 需要持續照顧有長期病患的親屬;
iv) 照顧者負荷指數達 7分或以上;
v)沒有經醫生診斷有精神病患或認知問題;
vi) 沒有嚴重的身體或精神問題;
vi)不是正接受心理治療;
vii) 兩年內沒有參加過正規的靜觀課程;
viii) 被照顧親屬並非剛離世;
ix) 三個月內沒有使用抗生素或益生菌
課堂詳情
時間：10月尾開始 星期三或四的 上午
地點：沙田瀝源健康院 - 本活動共8節, 每週1次, 每次1.5小時
兩組參加者均須在課程開始前、結束後，及結束後3個月填寫共次3問卷調查及提供3次糞便樣本。
*費用全免*
參與是次研究不需繳付任何費用。
每次提供樣本及填寫問卷將會獲得價值$100 的現金卷，最高可獲300元現金卷。
歡迎將以上資訊廣傳給親朋好友。
如需了解更多本研究資訊或查詢，請聯絡：
廖先生/魏先生 (研究助理)
電話：2252-8463  Whatsapp: 5264 6865
如有興趣參與研究，請使用以下連結報名。
報名：https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_8cu06nvBsZqwVBY
View Count
For request submissions, please submit them at
https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk

Announcements
[Earn up to HK$1100 cash] Recruiting participants aged 18 or above for Study on Sleep–Wake Patterns and Depressive Mood [最高可獲$1100現金] 誠邀18歲或以上人士參與作息模式與憂鬱情緒研究 - Psychology Department
From: Public Mental Health Laboratory
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
pmhlab@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -

【作息模式與憂鬱情緒研究】

成日夜晚瞓唔著，眼光光到天光？半夜又成日醒，醒咗又瞓唔返？
朝早覺得好倦，無動力去做野？又覺得情緒低落，無希望？
香港中文大學公共心理健康研究室現正進行一項有關作息型態及憂鬱情緒的研究。符合資格的參加者會於首4星期連續佩戴手錶式腕動計及完成評估問卷。 4星期後，研究人員會與參加者再次進行評估，符合資格的參加者將有機會獲得8-12節睡眠及作息治療，期間需要繼續佩戴手錶式腕動計及完成評估問卷。完成整個為期約14星期的研究後最高有機會總共獲得現金港幣$1100作為答謝金。
現誠邀符合以下條件的您參加研究：
18-65歲的香港居民
受憂鬱情緒及睡眠困擾的人士
能閱讀中文及理解廣東話
使用iOS/Android系統的智慧型電話
如有興趣參與，請填妥網上初步評估問卷（約5分鐘完成）：
https://esurvey.psy.cuhk.edu.hk/jfe/form/SV_ey6IheYeo7CLhRQ
研究人員將以電話/WhatsApp聯絡符合資格的參與者參加研究，並解釋研究計畫詳情。
如果有任何問題或想了解更多，歡迎與研究人員聯絡！
電話：3943 6575
WhatsApp：9405 4715
電郵：pmhlab@cuhk.edu.hk / evanpcy99@link.cuhk.edu.hk
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Study on Sleep–Wake Patterns and Depressive Mood

Do you often have trouble falling asleep at night?
Do you wake up frequently during the night and find it difficult to fall back asleep?
Do you feel exhausted in the morning and lack motivation to do things?
Do you often feel low in mood or hopeless?
The
Public Mental Health Laboratory at The Chinese University of Hong Kong
is conducting a research study on
sleep-wake patterns and depressive mood
.
Eligbible participants will be required to wear a
watch-type actigraphy device continuously for the first 4 weeks
and complete assessment surveys.
After 4 weeks, participants will undergo another assessment. Those who remain eligible may receive
8–12 sessions of sleep and circadian rhythm therapy
, during which they will continue wearing the actigraphy device and completing questionnaires.
Participants who complete the entire study (approximately
14 weeks
) may receive
up to HKD $1,100 in cash
as a token of appreciation.
We are now inviting individuals who meet the following criteria
Hong Kong residents aged 18–65
Experience depressive mood and sleep difficulties
Able to read Chinese and understand Cantonese
Use a smartphone with iOS or Android operating system
If you are interested, please complete the online preliminary screening questionnaire (about 5 minutes):
https://esurvey.psy.cuhk.edu.hk/jfe/form/SV_ey6IheYeo7CLhRQ
Research staff will contact eligible participants via
phone or WhatsApp
to explain the study details.
If you have any questions or would like to know more, feel free to contact us:
Phone: 3943 6575
WhatsApp: 9405 4715
Email: pmhlab@cuhk.edu.hk / evanpcy99@link.cuhk.edu.hk
View Count
For request submissions, please submit them at
https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:

2026-2027 Voluntary User-Pay Dental Service Scheme (VUPDSS)
Voluntary User-Pay Dental Service Scheme (VUPDSS) is a voluntary and self-paid dental service between the University’s members and the service providers, Health & Care Dental Services Limited and Quality HealthCare Dental Services Limited. Its primary purpose is to provide participants the additional convenience of receiving dental service at contracted dental clinics outside campus at concessionary rate. Full-time students, full-time staff and dependents, eligible retirees and dependents can enroll in the Scheme. The Scheme is open for application. Membership is valid from 1 September 2026 to 31 August 2027.
Details of the Scheme is available at:
https://www.umso.cuhk.edu.hk/form-download/
2026-2027 自費牙科服務計劃
「自費牙科服務計劃」為一個自願性付費形式的牙齒保健計劃。 合資格大學成員可參加由恒健牙科服務有限公司及卓健牙科服務有限公司所提供的牙科保健服務。 本計劃旨在為參加者提供一個具彈性及享有優惠價格之牙科服務。 全日制學生、全職職員及家屬、合資格退休員工及家屬均可參加。 計劃現正接受申請，會籍有效期由2026年9月1日至2027年8月31日。
計劃詳情，請瀏覽網頁:

From: Office of Co-operative Education Programme (OCEP)

coop@cuhk.edu.hk

[Co-op@CUHK Student Stories: Different Paths, Shared Growth!]
By bridging the gap between academic knowledge and real-world practice, the Co-operative Education Programme (Co-op@CUHK) enables students to gain hands-on experience across diverse industries, explore opportunities beyond their degree disciplines, and even take their learning beyond Hong Kong through non-local placements.
Whether you already have a clear career aspiration or are still exploring future possibilities, Co-op@CUHK offers a unique platform to discover your potential and develop professional competencies.
Check out the stories of our Co-op students and see how one experience can open doors to new opportunities, perspectives and possibilities for your future!
1. Turning Classroom Knowledge into Real-World Practice
2. Exploring Beyond My Major & Discovering New Possibilities
3.

輔導同行
聆聽傾訴 —
社區心理輔導服務
生活有時令人不堪重負，但你無須獨自面對。
香港中文大學教育心理學系「專業教育心理及輔導服務」現正推出心理輔導服務。由輔導碩士課程實習輔導員提供專業輔導，與你一同探索問題、梳理你的想法和感受，讓你找到適合你的方向和行動。
【服務詳情】
服務期：
2026 年 7 月至 12 月
服務地點：
何添樓101室
形式：
面對面輔導（每節 50 分鐘）
費用：
標準收費：HK$100 / 節
優惠收費：HK$30 / 節（適用於低收入或有特別需要人士）
對象：
正在尋求心理輔導之成年人（非緊急個案）
名額有限，先到先得。

【請立即網上報名】
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=6411435
如要查詢更多服務詳情，請致電3943 3413或電郵pepcs@cuhk.edu.hk查詢，我們會在辦公時間回覆您，謝謝。
Community Counselling Service: A Safe Space to be Heard
Life can be overwhelming, but you don't have to navigate it alone.
The Professional Educational Psychology and Counselling Service, under the Department of Educational Psychology at CUHK, is now offering accessible counselling services to support those in need. Our Master's counsellor trainees are here to provide a safe, non-judgmental space for you to explore your thoughts, feelings, and life challenges.
【Service Details
】
Service Period:
July – December 2026
Service Location:
Room 101, Ho Tim Building
Format:
Face-to-Face (50 minutes per session)
Fee:
Standard Rate: HK$100 / session
Subsidized Rate: HK$30 / session (For individuals with low income or special financial needs)
Target Audience:
Adults who are seeking counselling support (Non-urgent cases only)
Quota is limited and services are offered on a first-come, first-served basis.

【Register Online Now
】
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=6411435
For more service details, please call 3943 3413 or email pepcs@cuhk.edu.hk, we will reply you during office hours, thank you.

No vehicles except those pre-registered with the College Office will be allowed to enter or park at the College Piazza during this time.
For your safety, we kindly request that all individuals and pets refrain from entering the treated areas and avoid any direct contact with the surfaces for at least 24 hours following the completion of the work on 18 August 2026.

bodyText:

Announcements
Student Helpers Recruitment – School Liaison and Research Support  - SYEEM
From: Frankie Wong
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
frankiewong@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
JC GoAI
JC GoAI is a city-wide education project created and funded by The Hong Kong Jockey Club Charities Trust, in collaboration with the Chinese University of Hong Kong. In an era where generative AI is reshaping how we learn and work, JC GoAI aims to empower teachers to teach confidently using AI for all subjects, while nurturing AI literacy in students and cultivating them to learn creatively, effectively, and responsibly. With a comprehensive project design that emphasizes the ethical use of AI, we are ready to empower schools, teachers, and students to thrive in tomorrow’s AI-driven world. (Learn More: https://www.jcgoai.hk/). We are recruiting student helpers to provide school liaison and research support for the project.
Responsibilities:
Contact schools, teachers, students, and other project participants by telephone for project coordination and follow-up
Transcribe interview and research data in Cantonese, Chinese, or English
Assist with data cleaning, checking, matching, and the identification of missing, duplicated, or inconsistent records
Provide related research and administrative support as assigned
Maintain the confidentiality of all project and participant information
Requirements:
Current full-time undergraduate or postgraduate student at CUHK
Good command of spoken Cantonese and written Chinese and English
Clear and professional telephone communication skills
Careful attention to detail and the ability to work accurately with transcripts and datasets
Basic proficiency in Microsoft Excel or similar data-processing software
Student helper registration is required. Non-local students must hold a valid No Objection Letter
Immediate availability is preferred
Working Arrangement and Remuneration:
Flexible working hours, subject to the University's requirements
HKD 64 per hour
Application:
Please email your curriculum vitae and any relevant supporting documents to Dr. Liang at
siyaliang@cuhk.edu.hk

Responsibilities:
Contact schools, teachers, students, and other project participants by telephone for project coordination and follow-up
Transcribe interview and research data in Cantonese, Chinese, or English
Assist with data cleaning, checking, matching, and the identification of missing, duplicated, or inconsistent records
Provide related research and administrative support as assigned
Maintain the confidentiality of all project and participant information
Requirements:
Current full-time undergraduate or postgraduate student at CUHK
Good command of spoken Cantonese and written Chinese and English
Clear and professional telephone communication skills
Careful attention to detail and the ability to work accurately with transcripts and datasets
Basic proficiency in Microsoft Excel or similar data-processing software
Student helper registration is required. Non-local students must hold a valid No Objection Letter
Immediate availability is preferred
Working Arrangement and Remuneration:
Flexible working hours, subject to the University's requirements
HKD 64 per hour
Application:
Please email your curriculum vitae and any relevant supporting documents to Dr. Liang at
siyaliang@cuhk.edu.hk
https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
